His whole tall, broad form seemed made of solid bronze, and shaped in an unalterable mold, like Cellini's cast Perseus. Threading its way out from among his gray hairs, and continuing right down one side of his tawny, scorched face and neck until it disappeared into his clothing, you saw a slender, rod-like mark, livid and whitish. It resembled that vertical seam sometimes made in the straight, lofty trunk of a great tree when the lightning from above darts tearing down it, and, without wrenching off a single twig, peels and grooves out the bark from top to bottom before running off into the soil, leaving the tree still green and alive, but branded.
